name: Pale Greyish Blue
lede: Pale Greyish Blue is a light blue with a touch of grey, the kind of color dictionaries describe rather than name.

sections.title: Where the words appear
sections.body:
The name is descriptive: a pale blue, dulled with grey [3]. It is listed in the ISCC-NBS system of 1955 and in Ridgway's 1912 color book [3].

Paterson's dictionary uses the very same words to define another name, Botticelli blue, as a pale greyish-blue [1]. So the phrase is a description first, and the dictionary's own example shows how such descriptions get attached to a painter's name rather than a pigment [1]. Nearby colors in our data include [[powder-blue]] and [[light-blue]] [3].

The swatch on this page is #C5D8F6, the screen value we hold for it, which is an approximation and not a measured pigment [3]. Like any pale color it sits between its hue and [[white]], and because the name is a description and not a tradition, other lists may place it a little differently [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Pale Greyish Blue appears in 42 of the 23,781 paintings in our archive, about 0.18 percent, as photographed [2]. It is rarer than 56 percent of the named colors, and peaks in the 1800s, found in 16 of the 8,345 paintings from that century [2].
